messages:
nora (eng-runtime): AUTO-PAGER SEV2: Canary rollout for smart-routing policy is causing repeated region fallback churn and some clients are getting responses from the wrong model variant. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Incident 9127 created and assigned to sam (oncall). Alerts: variant_compat_error, increased p95 latency, cross-region retries.
sam (oncall): I'm on it. Which policy and canary id? Any immediate customer reports?
lee (sre): Policy: smart-route-prod-78, Canary id canary-78, canary % = 7%. Canary variant: model-gen-v4-q2, Stable: model-gen-v3. Telemetry shows a blob of requests still hitting nodes with prefix cache pointing to v4 qtable=q_v2 while the decode path expects q_v1 -> decode exceptions -> request fallback -> sticky routing causing oscillation between eu & us.
maria (product): Customer Ops seeing ~2% request failures (timeouts or bad completions) starting ~09:02 UTC. A few enterprise customers reported degraded latency. Not a full outage but visible.
ek (customer-ops): Posting in support: customers asking if we changed models. Need timeline to send to large customers.
sam (oncall): Can we get a sample log?
lee (sre): Sample:
```
[09:04:11] decoder ERROR: decode_exception: quant-table-mismatch expected=q_v1 got=q_v2 client=big-retailer
[09:04:11] routing WARN: fallback triggered to eu-west-1 (reason=decode_exception) sticky=true
[09:04:12] routing INFO: route reassigned -> us-east-1
[09:04:12] svc retry INFO: retry_count=2
```
lee (sre): Looks like sticky fallback entries weren't invalidated when the canary started, so some requests still tried v4 and failed, then policies kicked in and bounced traffic. That produced retries and latency spikes.
maria (product): Impact: p95 +300ms, 5xx up from 0.6% to 2.2% for embeddings/generation. Affected customers: multi-region deployment customers primarily.
ek (customer-ops): I'll prep a status note: "We're aware of increased errors/latency for certain customers; engineering investigating." ETA requested.
sam (oncall): Mitigation options ranked by speed:
1) Set policy sticky_fallback=false (global toggle) - quick.
2) Invalidate prefix-level cache on canary pool - medium.
3) Pause canary (set percent=0) - safe but needs rollout command.
4) Decrease routing-ttl for sticky entries to short window - quick but partial.
Which do we want now?
lee (sre): Plan: do 1 and 2 immediately. If errors persist, do 3. I'll run changes. Also push a temporary 'prefer-stable' flag so routing favors stable when decode exceptions are observed.
sam (oncall): Proceed. I'll notify Customer Ops and execs.
lee (sre): Commands to run:
```bash
redctl policy update smart-route-prod-78 --sticky_fallback=false --prefer_stable=true
redctl cache evict --pool=canary-pool-78 --pattern="canary:*"
redctl rollout set canary-78 --percent=0  # standby
```
lee (sre): Applied sticky_fallback=false at 09:07:02 UTC, prefer_stable=true applied. Cache eviction kicked off.
incident-bot: Action recorded: policy smart-route-prod-78 modified by lee; cache eviction task created.
sam (oncall): Customer Ops: send initial update saying we disabled sticky fallback and are cleaning cache; ETA 20-30m, will update.
ek (customer-ops): Status update posted 09:09 UTC. Linking to major customer tickets.
tess (oncall): I'm taking monitoring handoff for 45m. Sam -> tess. Watch p95 and cross-region retry rate. Alert if p95 > 1s or retries spike.
sam (oncall): Copy. Staying on exec sync.
lee (sre): Eviction done 09:14:40 UTC. Canary traffic auto-scaled down to 0% (rollout paused) at 09:15:30 because some autoscaler rule noticed decode errors and hit a safety gate. Early indicators: retries down 55%, 5xx back to ~0.9%.
maria (product): Good. We need a robust post-incident plan: immediate item to add a compatibility preflight for quant/decoder on variant swaps, and a deterministic cache invalidation event on variant promotion.
lee (sre): Agreed. Also propose adding a runtime 'compat-check' endpoint that can be run on a small synthetic traffic set to validate qtable and runtime kernel compatibility before enabling sticky routing for a new variant.
sam (oncall): I'll capture timeline and pager details for postmortem. Tess, keep monitors for another 30 minutes and close if stable.
tess (oncall): Monitoring stable at 09:42 UTC; p95 and 5xx returned to baseline. No further oscillations. Will close after confirming logs clear.
ek (customer-ops): Follow-up messages to customers sent with incident summary and mitigation steps. Some customers asked for a timeline of actions; they got it.
maria (product): I'll own the postmortem and action items. Agenda: root cause, code changes for compat-check, rollout gating, default sticky behavior for new canaries, and automation for cache eviction. Assign Lee for SRE fixes, Nora for runtime level changes.
lee (sre): Filing ticket SRE-1021 for cache-evict automation and SRE-1022 for prefer-stable fallback logic.
nora (eng-runtime): I'll add compat-check prototype and coordinate with product on rollout gating UX.
sam (oncall): Thanks everyone. Closing handoff to tess.
tess (oncall): Closing incident 09:47 UTC. Summary uploaded to incident tracker.
